details: Measured 27 Oct 19:04 local, the first hour with 6 lanes (owner, 27 Oct: "Давай 6 сразу"): 5 gate processes ran at once, load average 23.9 / 26.6 / 30.4 on 12 cores, and a quick gate that takes 7.2-8.4 minutes alone had run 36 minutes (about 4-5 times slower). Each gate runs the library tests in several processes itself, so the gates, not the agents (model calls use little CPU), saturate the Mac; the lanes then wait on each other at the gate and the 6 lanes may land no more than 2-3 would. Principle 2 (waste that repeats on every change).
failing_case: With 5 lanes reaching the gate together, each quick gate takes 30+ minutes instead of about 8.
pass_cases: Gates take a slot from a per-machine limit (a setting, default from the core count, for example 2 on 12 cores) and wait for a free one; the wait is printed with its reason.
Builds, reviews and checks are not limited by it.
Measured after: with 6 lanes, a gate takes no more than about 1.5 times its time alone, and the wait for a slot is shown in the gate log.
A test with a fake gate shows the third concurrent gate waits, and fails with the limit disabled.

findings.summary: Gates run all at once and slow each other down

details: CONFIRMED from the recorded measurement (handover, STATE 27 Oct early morning) and the fixer's report, which says the same.
This is a choice only the owner can make: latency per gate against gates per hour.
Introduction for the owner: relay lets only a few gates (the full test run before a merge) run at once on the Mac; the rest
wait their turn. The limit now comes from the core count: 12 cores give 2. Measured: one gate alone 7 min; two together 11.6 min
each; three together 17.6 min each. Two at once finish 10.3 gates an hour, one at a time 8.6, three 10.2.
Options: (a) 2 at once [recommended: 20% more gates per hour than 1, each gate 1.66x slower; the 1.5x target is moved to 1.7x];
(b) 1 at a time [each gate at its own speed, 1.5x met, 17% fewer gates per hour, the queue at the gate longer].
Size: 5 minutes for either (a constant or the item's text) plus one measurement when the Mac is free.
evidence: docs/handover.md:1345-1347 "Concurrent gates at 4 jobs: 1 = 8.6 gates/h, 2 at once 698 s each = 10.3/h, 3 at once 1058 s each = 10.2/h"
fixer report: "Not measured: after-number with 6 lanes (Mac loaded). Expected ~1.66x ... above the 1.5x pass case"
relay queue show gates-run-all-at-once-and-slow-each-other-down: pass case "no more than about 1.5 times its time alone"
failing_case: Item pass case 3: "with 6 lanes, a gate takes no more than about 1.5 times its time alone". Measured 27 Oct on this Mac (4 test
jobs): alone 420 s, 2 at once 698 s each = 1.66x, 3 at once 1058 s = 2.5x, 1 at a time 420 s (8.6 gates/h). With the new default
of 2 on 12 cores, two gates run together at about 698 s plus the load of 6 lanes' agents and quiet checks; expected >= 1.66x,
not <= 1.5x. The fixer did not measure the after-number (the Mac was loaded; the brief allowed "not measured").
fix_hint: Ask the owner; on (a) record the measured number and the revised bound in the queue item; on (b) set CORES_PER_SLOT to 12.
pass_cases: 1. Owner picks 2 slots: the item's pass case is restated as "a gate takes no more than about 1.7x its time alone" (or the wait
included), and one measured after-number with 6 lanes is recorded in the item.
2. Owner picks 1 slot: CORES_PER_SLOT (or the formula) gives 1 on 12 cores; a gate runs at about 420 s; throughput 8.6 gates/h.
3. Either way: RELAY_GATE_SLOTS still overrides, and the third concurrent gate test still waits with 2 slots set.
reason: Owner choice (2 slots vs 1, 1.66x vs 1.5x) left open by the fixer; after-number not measured. Recommend 2 slots with the bound restated.
findings.summary: the default of 2 slots is expected to give 1.66x a gate's time alone, above the item's 1.5x pass case, and the after-number was not measured

details: CONFIRMED by reading take_slot: each process opens slot-0..count-1 of its own count, so the effective machine limit is the largest
count among running gates. Pre-existing for the env value, but this change advertises the variable as the way to set the limit
and is the item that asked for a per-machine setting. Rated LOW: the default (no variable) is the same on every gate of one
machine, so ordinary use is correct; a per-machine config is a new mechanism and goes to the design track if wanted.
Size: 15 minutes for "the count is the minimum of the own count and a count file the setting writes", or a queue item.
